CFL Coverage Reference
CFL Coverage Reference Guide

This guide is a reference tool for identifying and tagging defensive coverage shells in Canadian Football League (CFL) film. It is designed for data coders working in a PFF-style tagging system and covers the full range of zone and man coverage families used in modern Canadian football.

Purpose

This guide exists to ensure consistent, accurate coverage tagging across all coders. Each coverage entry includes the shell diagram, key identification cues, and CFL-specific notes that differ from American football conventions.

How to Use

Navigate using the tabs above. Each coverage family has its own tab. Within each tab, click a coverage card to expand its identification notes, and use the View Diagram button to pull up the shell diagram in a modal viewer. Use the search bar to find a specific coverage by name or keyword.

Hold vs. Cut

The most important CFL-specific distinction in Cover 3. Hold means the cornerbacks own the deep outside thirds and the halfbacks play the curl-flat low zones. Cut means the halfbacks own the deep thirds alongside the FS, while the corners play low zone with a built-in cut-and-carry pattern match on any vertical routes.

Tampa-2 Classification

To classify a coverage as Tampa-2, the middle-of-field hole defender must be an inside linebacker by listed roster position. If a free safety drops to the middle of the field — regardless of alignment — it is classified as Cover 3 Cut, not Tampa-2.

Coverage Families
  • Cover 2 Two-deep zone or man — relatively rare in CFL due to field width
  • Cover 3 Hold Standard Cover 3, corners own deep thirds
  • Cover 3 Cut Halfbacks deep, corners play low with cut & carry
  • Cover 4 Quarters — most common deep shell in modern CFL
  • Man Cover 0, 10, 11, 12 — all man-coverage variants
Personnel & Alignment (CFL)

Base CFL defenses have 4 down linemen, 3 linebackers (MIKE, WILL, SAM), and 5 defensive backs — Boundary Corner (BC), Field Corner (FC), Boundary Halfback (BH), Field Halfback (FH), and Free Safety (FS). When teams drop to three linemen, they add either a 6th defensive back (dimeback) or an extra linebacker (names vary by team — commonly called Buck or Jack). Position abbreviations used in this guide reflect the DB-heavy base alignment standard across the CFL.

2 Cover 2 Zone / Man
Cover 2 Man
  • Same structure as American Cover 2 Man
  • Most common form of Cover 2 in Canadian football
  • Defenders will often press on the line, especially the corners and halfbacks
  • Defenders will play catch-man and trail receivers in coverage to utilize their over-the-top help
ManPress
Cover 2 Zone
  • Same structure as American Cover 2 Zone with one key difference
  • It's very challenging to cover the full width of the CFL field with just two deep defenders. Therefore, corners will have carry responsibility attached to their flats zone to help them out
  • Corners will sink as they read the #2 receiver
    • If #2 runs out to the flats, the corner stays in the flats
    • If #2 runs vertical, the corner locks on to #1 and carries him out of the flats — this allows the deep half player to ignore the outermost area of the field and play overtop of #2
  • Because of this, there will often be multiple players responsible for the flats. With 6 underneath defenders: 2 flats, 2 curl/flats, 2 hook/curls. The curl/flat players will cover the flats if the initial flat defender has to carry a vertical route
  • TAMPA NOTE: To classify a coverage as Tampa-2, the middle-of-field defender must be an inside linebacker by listed roster position. If a free safety lines up at a LB position and drops to the middle, it is classified as Cover 3 Cut — not Tampa
ZoneRare in CFL
3 Cover 3 — Hold Zone
Cover 3 Hold
  • Standard Cover 3. Hold means the outside deep thirds are covered by the cornerbacks, while the halfbacks are responsible for the curl-flat low zones
  • Halfbacks should be rerouting any vertical routes that come at them in order to help the corners out
  • MIKE linebacker is hole player but is tied to tailback release. If the tailback free releases in a direction, MIKE LB will open that direction and cheat that way in order to help any in-breaking routes as hole player
Zone
Cover 3 Hold w/ Lock
  • Some teams will run base Hold but play man ("lock") on one outside receiver
  • In this case, the halfback on that side will take over the deep third behind the lock defender. The halfback will naturally cheat towards the middle of the field, knowing a vertical route will be covered by the lock defender
  • This puts a little more strain on the SAM and MIKE linebackers having to move out a zone, but similarly with the outside receiver locked, it naturally narrows the field
ZoneLock (Man)
Cover 3 Hold — Pattern Match (3-Seam)
  • Guide on how teams will read out routes in order to pattern match in Hold (equivalent to 3-Seam in American football)
  • SAM and WILL will be inside wallers and take first in-breaking routes and pick up in man
  • Boundary halfback reads 2 to 1 — if #2 goes vertical, he picks up in man (the Curl-Flat seam adjustment in AC)
  • Field halfback reads 3 to 2 — if #3 goes to flats he follows; if #3 goes vertical he sinks with outside leverage; if #3 goes inside he sinks overtop of #2
ZonePattern Match
3 Cover 3 — Cut (aka Double Cloud) Zone
Cover 3 Cut
  • In "Cut", the halfbacks are responsible for the deep thirds (along with the FS) and the corners are low zone players. This is the Canadian equivalent of double cloud
  • Cut & Carry Corner: The most important distinction of Cut is that every cut call has pattern-matching built in to the corner position. A corner in Cut should sink off the snap as they read the inside receivers while staying atop a potential vertical route by #1
  • If someone inside breaks out to the flats, the corner will jump on it. If no receiver breaks to the flats, the corner will carry the vertical route from #1 — effectively playing man on that player and turning the coverage into more of a Cover 4. But it's important to understand that it's still a Cover 3 call
ZoneCut & Carry
4 Cover 4 (Quarters) Zone
Cover 4 — Base Quarters
  • Base quarters coverage look — plays out very similar to American football Quarters albeit with an extra underneath defender (usually)
  • Base Quarters always has the boundary corner and boundary halfback on one side of the deep quarters, and the Free Safety and field corner on the other side
  • This allows the field halfback to cover the curl/flat zone on the wider side of the field, to make it easier to cover that space
  • Similar to other coverages, the MIKE's opening direction is tied to the tailback. While he is a hook/curl player, he will open and cheat in the direction of the tailback opening to help with the new receiver to that side
Zone
Cover 4 Weak
  • While this used to be an adjustment, it's now become the most prevalent form of Quarters in the CFL
  • The boundary halfback is now responsible for the curl/flat zone. The FS rotates to the boundary inside quarter, while the SAM linebacker drops to the field inside quarter. MIKE is responsible for the hook/curl zone that SAM previously covered, and WILL is the other hook/curl player, tied to the TB's release direction
  • Has become more common because of hashmark narrowing. Now the boundary side is much wider, making it very challenging to ask the WILL linebacker to cover the flats on a quick boundary throw. Keeping the halfback low allows the defense to react quicker
Zone
Cover 4 Double Trap
  • A disguise coverage designed to look like Cut coverage pre-snap. Both halfbacks are dropping, with a middle-of-field safety. The SAM linebacker also drops into the inside quarter and leaves both corners free to sit in the flats
  • The idea is to trick the QB into thinking the corners are playing Cut and carry — so they will sink on any outside vertical. However, because there are four deep defenders, the corners know they have help over the top and have no vertical responsibility at all. They are only playing the flats and will jump any quick outs to the sidelines
  • MIKE has a tough ask here, needing to cover the hook/curl zone vacated by the SAM LB dropping into the deep quarter
Zone
Cover 4 Field Lock
  • A rare coverage against four receivers to one side and one to another
  • The field corner will lock on the outside receiver and the rest of the defense will simply play Cover 4 above him
  • Sometimes used near the endzone when zones get tightened — helps counter a slant from the outside receiver underneath 3 clearout routes from the inside receivers
ZoneLock (Man)Situational
Cover 4 Quad Box
  • A pattern-matching Cover 4 adjustment that teams make when there are four receivers to one side and one to another
  • On the one-receiver side (almost always the boundary side) the corner will simply play man on that receiver
  • The boundary halfback will then play the outside deep quarter but knows he can cheat to the middle of the field more because of boundary sideline coverage. WILL LB has curl/flats to that side but often will man on TB if he free releases boundary
  • The field side players form a 5-man box over the four receivers: SAM plays low outside zone, MIKE plays low inside zone, FC plays high outside zone, FH plays high middle zone, and FS plays high inside zone

0 Man Coverage Man
Cover 0 (Zero)
  • All out blitz, everyone in man with no help over the top
  • Used more than you would think in the CFL, especially near the endzone
  • If an eligible receiver stays in to pass block, his coverage player will either drop into coverage or rush the quarterback (often defensive backs drop, linebackers rush)
ManBlitz
Cover 10 (One-Oh)
  • Classic Cover 1 behind a blitzing linebacker
  • One deep free player, everyone else in man — not overly uncommon in the CFL
  • Defenders should play with inside leverage to force the QB into making tougher outside throws
ManBlitz
Cover 11 (One-One)
  • Classic man coverage with one zone player at each level of the field. Four pass rushers, eight coverage players
  • Oftentimes linebackers will have a green dog tag and rush if their man stays in to block
  • Defenders should play with outside leverage on receivers
Man
Cover 12 (One-Two)
  • One deep free, two hole players, man everywhere else
  • Used sparingly in pass-heavy situations in the CFL
  • Sometimes used to take away quick slants with two hole players dropping into that space to force the QB to look elsewhere
